title: Wise AI in four questions
subtitle: Draft answers from the Wise AI briefing, with what wisdom traditions offer on each.
footer: Rufus Pollock · Wise AI briefing · Draft, October 2026
alt: Mindmap. How should we approach the development of AI wisely, and what do wisdom traditions offer? Alignment: partly, and not yet in a way anyone can check. Risk and pace: go at the speed of wisdom, slow the frontier, speed up safety. Broader impacts: AI's deepest effect is on our capacity to choose well; keep it a servant. Consciousness: we do not know and may never; relate with humility, low-cost care and clear honesty. Each with three or four supporting points, including what wisdom traditions offer.

root.label: How should we approach AI wisely?
root.note: And what do wisdom traditions offer?

children.label: Alignment
children.text: Partly, and not yet in a way anyone can check.
Aligned should mean good, which includes wise.
Today's methods: mostly good, hard to verify.
Goodness can be cultivated, not specified.
Traditions: a richer target and a model of formation.

children.label: Risk and pace
children.text: Go at the speed of wisdom: slow the frontier, speed up safety.
children.note: If we can't be sure, how fast should we go?

children.text: The risks are real and contested.
The world races: a collective action trap.
Slow and steer; far more people should decide.
Traditions: restraint, strongest on will and process.

children.label: Broader impacts
children.text: AI's deepest effect is on our capacity to choose well; keep it a servant.
children.note: Setting catastrophe aside, how should we live with AI?

children.text: Its default pull weakens agency and judgment.

children.label: Consciousness (minor)
children.text: We do not know and may never; relate with humility, low-cost care and clear honesty.
The evidence is weak either way.
Traditions ask: is there feeling that can suffer?
